historical_references.reference: Fanibhusan Chattopadhyay was a renowned scholar and social reformer from Bengal, India. He was born in the village of Chironton, in the Hooghly district, in 1861. Fanibhusan is best known for his efforts to eradicate child marriage and promote widow remarriage in Bengali society. He founded the 'Brahmachari Ashram' in 1895, which became a model for other ashrams that followed. Fanibhusan passed away in 1940.

Fanibhusan Debi was a 17th-century poet and philosopher from Bengal, India. He is considered one of the greatest poets of the Bengali language. Fanibhusan Debi's most famous work is the poem 'Mohabhava Mala', which explores the themes of love, devotion, and spirituality. He was also a major figure in the development of the 'Bhakti movement' in Bengal, which emphasized the importance of personal devotion to God. Fanibhusan Debi passed away in 1666.
